title: Congruence and Similarity: Similar Triangles and Scale Factors
seo_title: Sec 2 Congruence and similarity Worksheets: Free Secondary 2 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: congruent figures; similar figures; properties of similar triangles and polygons: corresponding angles are equal, corresponding sides are proportional; enlargement and reduction of a plane figure; solving simple problems involving congruence and similarity
meta_desc: Free Secondary 2 similarity and congruence worksheets: congruence conditions SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS, scale factors, missing sides in similar triangles and shapes, and shadow and model problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Similar shapes: equal angles, and every length × the same scale factor.
key_sub: Congruent triangles match by SSS, SAS, ASA or RHS. AAA only proves similarity.
body_html:
How it works

Congruent shapes are identical in shape and size. Two triangles are congruent if they match by SSS, SAS, ASA or RHS.

Similar shapes have equal angles and every length is multiplied by the same scale factor. Scale factor = new length ÷ matching old length.

Example

Two similar shapes have matching sides 4 cm and 10 cm. Another side of the small shape is 6 cm. Find the matching side.

Scale factor = 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5.

6 × 2.5 = 15.

Answer: 15 cm

Example

Are a 3 × 5 rectangle and a 6 × 9 rectangle similar?

6 ÷ 3 = 2 but 9 ÷ 5 = 1.8.

Answer: No

Common mistakes

  • Adding the difference instead of multiplying: from 4 to 10 is × 2.5, not + 6.
  • Using the scale factor the wrong way round when going from the large shape to the small one.
  • Thinking three equal angles (AAA) prove congruence. They only prove similarity.
  • Matching the wrong pair of sides. Match sides opposite equal angles.

faq.q: What is the difference between similar and congruent?
faq.a: Congruent shapes are identical in size and shape. Similar shapes are the same shape, but one can be an enlargement of the other.

faq.q: What are the conditions for congruent triangles?
faq.a: SSS (three sides), SAS (two sides and the included angle), ASA (two angles and a side) and RHS (right angle, hypotenuse and a side).

faq.q: How do I find a missing side in similar shapes?
faq.a: Find the scale factor from a pair of matching sides, then multiply (or divide) the side you know.

faq.q: Why does AAA not prove congruence?
faq.a: Triangles with the same angles can be different sizes, so they are similar but not always congruent.

items.q: Two triangles each have sides 6 cm and 8 cm with a 50° angle between them. Are they congruent?
items.e: Two sides and the included angle: SAS.

items.q: A shape is reflected. Is the image congruent to the original?
c: Only if the mirror line is vertical
items.e: Reflection keeps all lengths and angles, so yes.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? Two angles and a side that is not between them are equal (AAS).
items.e: This is ASA.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? All three sides of one triangle are equal to all three sides of the other.
items.e: This is SSS.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? Both have a right angle, equal hypotenuses and one other equal side.
items.e: This is RHS.

items.q: Triangle 1 has sides 5, 7, 9 cm. Triangle 2 has sides 9, 5, 7 cm. Are they congruent?
c: No, the sides are in a different order
items.e: The same three side lengths in any order: yes, by SSS.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? Two sides and the angle between them are equal.
items.e: This is SAS.

items.q: Both triangles have angles 40°, 60° and 80°. Are they definitely congruent?
c: No, because the angles are different
No — they are similar, but could be different sizes
items.e: Equal angles only prove the triangles are the same shape: similar, not necessarily congruent.

items.q: Two right-angled triangles both have a hypotenuse of 13 cm and a side of 5 cm. Are they congruent?
c: Only if they face the same way
items.e: Right angle, hypotenuse, side: RHS.

items.q: Which of these does NOT prove two triangles are congruent?
items.e: Three equal angles only show the triangles are similar: AAA.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent. Which condition is this? Two angles and the side between them are equal.
items.e: This is ASA.

items.q: Which word means “exactly the same shape and size”?
items.e: Congruent shapes are identical in shape and size.

items.q: Which word means “the same shape but possibly a different size”?
items.e: Similar shapes have equal angles and proportional sides.

items.q: Two triangles have all three angles equal. They must be…
items.e: Equal angles prove they are similar.

items.q: Triangle ABC has AB = 5 cm, BC = 7 cm and angle B = 40°. Triangle PQR has PQ = 5 cm, QR = 7 cm and angle Q = 40°. Why are they congruent?

items.q: Two triangles each have angles 50° and 60° and the side between them is 8 cm. Why are they congruent?
items.e: Two angles and the side between them: ASA.

items.q: Two triangles have sides 4, 5, 6 cm and 4, 5, 6 cm. Why are they congruent?
items.e: Three sides equal: SSS.

items.q: What does RHS stand for?
items.e: Right angle, Hypotenuse, Side.

items.q: A triangle is rotated 90°. Is the image congruent to the original?
c: It is similar but not congruent
items.e: Rotations keep size and shape: yes.

items.q: A triangle is enlarged by scale factor 2. Is the image congruent to the original?
c: No, it is a different shape
items.e: The sides are doubled, so it is similar, not congruent.

items.q: Rectangle A is 3 cm by 6 cm. Rectangle B is 7.5 cm by 17 cm. Are they similar?
c: Yes, because all the angles are 90°
No, the sides are not multiplied by the same number
items.e: 7.5 ÷ 3 = 2.5 and 17 ÷ 6 = None. The scale factors differ, so they are not similar.

Yes, both sides are multiplied by 2

items.q: A 1.5 m post casts a 2 m shadow. At the same time a tree casts a 12 m shadow. How tall is the tree?
items.e: Scale factor 12 ÷ 2 = 6. 1.5 × 6 = 9 m.

items.q: A photo 10 cm by 15 cm is enlarged so that the short side is 25 cm. How long is the long side?
items.e: Scale factor 2.5. 15 × 2.5 = 37.5 cm.

Two similar triangles have corresponding angles. One triangle has angles 35°, 65° and 80°. What are the angles of the other?
c: They depend on the scale factor
items.e: Similar shapes have equal angles; only the lengths change.

items.q: In similar triangles, which statement is always true?
items.e: Similar means same shape: corresponding angles are equal.

items.q: Are all squares similar?
c: Only if their sides are whole numbers
Only if they are the same size
items.e: Every square has 90° angles and sides in the ratio 1 : 1, so yes.

items.q: Are all rectangles similar?
c: Only if one is double the other
Only if they have the same area
items.e: A 1 × 2 rectangle and a 1 × 5 rectangle are different shapes, so no.

items.q: A triangle has sides 3, 4 and 5 cm. A similar triangle has its shortest side 9 cm. What is its longest side?
items.e: Scale factor 3. 5 × 3 = 15 cm.

items.q: A map uses a scale of 1 : 25 000. A lake is 3.2 cm long on the map. How long is it in real life?
In triangle ABC, DE is parallel to BC. AD = 4 cm, AB = 10 cm and DE = 6 cm. How long is BC?
items.e: Triangles ADE and ABC are similar with scale factor 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5. BC = 6 × 2.5 = 15 cm.

items.q: Triangle P has two sides of 6 cm with an angle of 60° between them. Triangle Q has three sides of 6 cm. Are they congruent?
c: No — Q has no angles given
Only if they face the same way
Yes — P is also equilateral with sides of 6 cm
No — P has only two sides given
items.e: P is isosceles with a 60° angle between the equal sides, so all its angles are 60° and its third side is also 6 cm. Yes, they are congruent (SSS).

items.q: A shape is enlarged by scale factor 3. What happens to the perimeter?
items.e: All lengths × 3, so the perimeter × 3.

items.q: A door 2 m tall is shown as 4 cm on a plan. What is the scale?
A person 1.8 m tall stands 4 m from a lamp post and has a 2 m shadow. How tall is the lamp post?
items.e: The big triangle's base is 4 + 2 = 6 m, which is 3 times the 2 m shadow. 1.8 × 3 = 5.4 m.

items.q: Two similar cylinders have heights 6 cm and 9 cm. The smaller has radius 4 cm. What is the radius of the larger?
items.e: Scale factor 1.5. 4 × 1.5 = 6 cm.

items.q: Which pair of triangles must be similar?
c: Two triangles with a side of 5 cm
items.e: Equal angles mean similar.

items.q: A rectangle 4 cm by 6 cm is similar to one that is 10 cm by y cm, where 10 cm matches 4 cm. Find y.
items.e: Scale factor 2.5. y = 6 × 2.5 = 15 cm.

items.q: Congruent shapes are…
c: the same shape but a different size
the same area but any shape
exactly the same shape and size
items.e: Congruent means exactly the same shape and size (they may be reflected or rotated).

items.q: A triangle with sides 6, 8 and 10 cm is reduced by scale factor ½. What are the new sides?
items.e: Halve every side: 3, 4 and 5 cm.

items.q: The scale factor from shape A to shape B is 4. What is the scale factor from B to A?
items.e: Going back divides by 4, so the scale factor is ¼.
